nodes.text: Add (NH4)2S to sample_with_HCl to test for sulfide-forming cations (Cu2+, Cd2+, Zn2+)

support.quote: I will use (NH4)2S to test for the presence of cations that form sulfides, such as Cu2+, Cd2+, and Zn2+, which are insoluble in acidic conditions.

nodes.text: Cu2+ is present (black sulfide precipitate; Pb2+ ruled out because HCl dissolved precipitate)

support.quote: The formation of a black precipitate upon adding (NH4)2S suggests the presence of cations that form black sulfides, such as Cu2+ or Pb2+. Since the addition of HCl dissolved any precipitate initially, Pb2+ is unlikely, leaving Cu2+ as a probable candidate.

hypothesis.canonical: Cu2+ is present in the sample

nodes.text: Add NH4SCN to test for Fe3+ (blood-red complex with thiocyanate)

support.quote: I will use NH4SCN to test for the presence of Fe3+, which forms a blood-red complex with thiocyanate.

nodes.text: Adding NH4SCN: precipitate unchanged; supernatant turns red-orange

support.quote: 'result': 'The amount and color of the existing precipitate does not noticeably change.\nColor of the supernatant solution changes to red-orange.'

nodes.text: Red-orange supernatant with NH4SCN confirms Fe3+ presence; black precipitate confirms Cu2+

support.quote: The change in color of the supernatant solution to red-orange upon adding NH4SCN indicates the presence of Fe3+, which forms a complex with thiocyanate. The black precipitate suggests the presence of Cu2+.
